text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL NEGOTIATES TO CONTAIN DEFICIT
In its diplomatic efforts to contain the trade deficit, Brazil was able to negotiate more favorable tariff conditions with China for imports of soybean, orange juice and coffee.
-- DIRECT INVESTMENT AMOUNTS TO $5.9 BLN
Brazil received $5.9 billion in direct foreign investment in the first five months of 1997, up 82.1 percent from the same period last year.
-- BRAZILIAN BANKS BET ON RUSSIA
Brazilian banks are increasingly interested in the Russian market because of high returns on Russian bonds and low prices of local shares.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- INQUIRY CITES CRIMES IN BONDS SCANDAL
The final report on a corruption scandal involving state and municipal bonds will hold governors and mayors responsible for the crime of misappropriating public funds.
-- GUSTAVO KUERTEN GOES TO SEMIFINAL
Brazilian tennis player Gustavo Kuerten, who beat his Russian opponent by three sets to two, is the first Brazilian to reach a Grand Slam semifinal.
O GLOBO
-- LIST OF BAND B QUALIFIERS TO BE PUBLISHED TODAY
The Communications Ministry will announce today the list of consortia which qualify for cellular telephone Band B concessions.
-- RIO BUILDING OCCUPIED BY 70 HOMELESS
Seventy homeless people have invaded and occupied a building in Rio de Janeiro which belongs to Banco Meridional and has been empty for 15 years.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
